subject: Follow-up: Local data routing impact on hosting choice (recap + next steps)
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Novak <elena.novak@medifin.eu>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T14:08:00+00:00
Subject: Post-call recap — residency & cross-region routing constraints (next steps)

Hi Elena — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the tech dive: 

Summary of customer constraints (as discussed)
- Primary requirement: All customer PII and transaction data must remain in EU jurisdiction at rest and in transit (no backups outside EU unless encrypted and with explicit controls).
- Secondary requirement: APAC user traffic must see sub-120ms median tail latency where possible; acceptable to route APAC reads to a nearby regional endpoint if EU-hosted writes are required.
- Ops constraint: minimal changes to existing KMS footprint — you prefer to bring your own KMS or authorize a customer-managed key.

What Redwood heard as possible fit
- Private VPC (Redwood Private) gives the clearest compliance posture (customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM integration, no egress outside EU).
- Dedicated capacity (Reserved) could work if we can guarantee that backups, snapshots, and fallbacks remain in EU; we'd need to lock region affinity and explicit routing rules.
- Hosted API is attractive for speed of rollout but will need region gating and a hardened fallback policy to avoid cross-border backups.

Immediate asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm whether encrypted backups to an AWS EU region (e.g., eu-west-1) are acceptable, or whether backups must be logically wiped after X days? (see attachment: 20261118-mediFin-data-requirements.pdf)
2) We will prepare a short comparison table (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) mapping controls, latency expectations, and cost/ops tradeoffs.
3) Technical deep-dive: propose Tue Nov 24 at 09:00 CET — will include infra/serving engineers to validate routing and KMS integration.

Attachments: 20261118-mediFin-data-requirements.pdf (uploaded summary from our call)

Thanks — I’ll coordinate the calendar once you confirm the preferred time.

Best,
Grace O'Connor

Redwood Inference

From: Elena Novak <elena.novak@medifin.eu>

Cc: MediFin IT <it@medifin.eu>
Date: 2026-11-19T08:12:00+01:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — residency & cross-region routing constraints (next steps)

Thanks Grace — helpful recap. A few clarifications from compliance and infra teams (copied to IT):

- Backups: All backups and snapshots must remain in EU. We cannot accept backups stored outside EU even if encrypted.
- DR copies: Disaster recovery copies may be stored outside EU only after explicit legal approval; for now assume DR must also be EU-located.
- APAC latency: We have a mixed user base — approx 8% of traffic from APAC. Median latency target for APAC is 120ms but 95th percentile should not exceed 250ms for typical inference calls.
- KMS: We prefer to bring our own KMS (AWS KMS with key policies) or use Redwood-managed keys under strict contract terms.

Please include SOC2 / audit evidence in the package for the Nov 24 session (we need to vet controls). I attached our internal requirements spreadsheet (medifin-internal-reqs.xlsx).

Given these constraints, our security lead is leaning toward Private VPC, but the procurement team wants a clear cost/time tradeoff against Dedicated reserved capacity.

Elena Novak
Head of Platform Security
MediFin Labs
elena.novak@medifin.eu

Subject: Re: Post-call recap — residency & cross-region routing constraints (next steps)

Elena — appreciate the details and the spreadsheet. Quick proposals so procurement and security can evaluate tradeoffs: 

1) Private VPC (recommended for strict compliance)
   - Pros: Isolated control plane, customer-managed networking, KMS/HSM integration, no cross-border backups by default.
   - Cons: Longer lead time for on-prem/VPC setup, higher initial integration effort and support scope; pricing is licensing + support.

2) Dedicated Reserved (fast-to-provision, EU-only pool)
   - Pros: Predictable throughput, reserved GPU capacity locked to EU regions, faster onboarding than Private.
   - Cons: Must contractually enforce backup/replication restrictions; we can provide region affinity and automated snapshot lifecycle policies to keep snapshots in EU.

3) Hosted API (not recommended as a first choice given current constraints)
   - Pros: Lowest friction, Redwood-managed updates and autoscaling.
   - Cons: Requires strict policy gating for backups and would need a dedicated EU-only tenancy to pass your controls.

Action items from Redwood:
- I attached a short brief comparing controls and expected timeline: hosting-options-brief.pdf.
- We'll surface our SOC2 summary and evidence package during the Nov 24 session (link: https://drive.redwood.ai/s/hosting-options-comparison-20261119).
- Proposed pilot: Dedicated EU pool for a 30-day performance/latency test using a mirror of non-sensitive traffic, followed by Private VPC for production if compliance requires.

Can you confirm whether procurement would accept a staged approach (Dedicated pilot -> Private prod)? If so, we can include estimated TTM and costs in the procurement packet.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
